S1.2 # of civil society organisations and community led organisations with increased capacity to advocate for the rights of key populations

description.narrative: This indicator aims to measure the extent to which Love Alliance investments have increased the capacity of civil society organisations and community-led organisations to advocate for the rights of key populations at the national, sub-national, regional or sub-regional level.

comment.narrative: Investments in civil society capacity building have been substantial in Zimbabwe, with external donors/programs including the Global Fund, PEPFAR, PITCH, and others supporting organisational capacity building. The Right Here, Right Now Platform supported by Rutgers has also provided advocacy support

24 organisations were capacitated in Advocacy and Financial Sustainability. Of these 24, 3 were capacitated in 2021 and 21 in 2022. From the total of 24 organisations, 19 are LGBTI Led and Oriented, 4 are Sex Worker Led and 1 was People who use and inject drugs oriented. There were no organisations capacitated in 2023In 2024 3 community led organisation were also trained and these include Saywhat, Students Network and Leonard Cheshire Disability Network

description.narrative: This indicator aims to measure the number policies, laws and strategies that are newly being implemented to better meet the needs of key populations as a result of Love Alliance support.

comment.narrative: Two government strategies are being implemented to meet the needs of key populations. The Zimbabwe National HIV and AIDS Strategic Plan IV which was launched in 2021 and the Zimbabwe National Master Drug Plan which was developed in 2022. Both documents acknowledge LGBTI persons and their developmental issues specifically MSM

description.narrative: This indicator aims to measure the number of policies related to improved civic space and freedoms or decriminalisation of key populations, that are formally proposed or accepted with Love Alliance support

comment.narrative: There are no policies formally proposed/accepted (bills, bonds, ballot measures, regulations, administrative policies etc.) which improve the civic space for decriminilisation. Rather two bills were introduced to restrict further the space namely the Private Voluntary Organisations Bill and the Patroitic Bill (which is an amendment of the Criminal Codification and Law Reform Act)
